newsitem.title: UK: UK government backs SIB on equity borrowing rules.
newsitem.headline: UK government backs SIB on equity borrowing rules.

text.p: The government said on Friday it fully accepted a Securities and Investments Board (SIB) recommendation that there is no immediate need to tighten or extend regulation of equity stock borrowing and repos.

As a result, the way is now clear for parliament to consider proposals in the finance bill for a sweeping reform of the current fiscal regime as it affects the lending and borrowing of equities, Economic Secretary to the Treasury Angela Knight said.
"These proposals amount to a substantial liberalisation and modernisation of existing tax rules.

"Taken together with the SIB's proposed light regulatory touch, they should enhance the competitive development of this market, to the benefit of investors and market intermediaries alike," Knight said in a written parliamentary answer.

She said the SIB, in a report requested by the government, also proposed carrying out further work on stock borrowing to cover guidance on good practice, the disclosure regime for short selling and the stock borrowing regime for smaller companies.
